passages.text: When David had gone a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him. He had a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David traveled a little past the top of the hill.
Ziba was the servant of Mephibosheth.
Ziba came to meet David.
Ziba brought two donkeys.
The donkeys had saddles.
Ziba loaded the donkeys with food and drink.
He brought two hundred loaves of bread.
He brought one hundred clusters of raisins.
He brought one hundred summer fruits.
He brought a skin of wine.
passages.original: וְדָוִ֗ד עָבַ֤ר מְעַט֙ מֵֽהָרֹ֔אשׁ וְהִנֵּ֥ה צִיבָ֛א נַ֥עַר מְפִי־ בֹ֖שֶׁת לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וְצֶ֨מֶד חֲמֹרִ֜ים חֲבֻשִׁ֗ים וַעֲלֵיהֶם֩ מָאתַ֨יִם לֶ֜חֶם וּמֵאָ֧ה צִמּוּקִ֛ים וּמֵ֥אָה קַ֖יִץ וְנֵ֥בֶל יָֽיִן׃

passages.text: “Why do you have these?” asked the king. Ziba replied, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”
passages.sermon:
King David saw Ziba.
David was the king of Israel.
Ziba was the servant of Mephibosheth.
David asked Ziba a question.
David said, “Why do you have these things?”
Ziba answered David.
Ziba said, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride.”
Ziba said, “The bread and the summer fruit are for the young men to eat.”
Ziba said, “The wine is for anyone who becomes tired in the wilderness to drink.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־ צִיבָ֖א מָה־ אֵ֣לֶּה לָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר צִ֠יבָא הַחֲמוֹרִ֨ים לְבֵית־ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לִרְכֹּ֗ב וּלְהַלֶּחֶם וְהַקַּ֙יִץ֙ לֶאֱכ֣וֹל הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְהַיַּ֕יִן לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת הַיָּעֵ֖ף בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: “Where is your master’s grandson?” asked the king. And Ziba answered, “Indeed, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he has said, ‘Today, the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather.’ ”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Ziba.
David was the king of Israel.
Ziba was the servant of Mephibosheth.
David asked Ziba a question.
David said, “Where is your master’s grandson?”
Ziba answered the king.
Ziba said, “He is in Jerusalem.”
Ziba explained why Mephibosheth stayed in Jerusalem.
Ziba said, “He said, ‘Today the house of Israel will give me back the kingdom of my grandfather.’”
Mephibosheth was the grandson of Saul, the former king.
Mephibosheth hoped to receive the kingdom again.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאַיֵּ֖ה בֶּן־ אֲדֹנֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר צִיבָ֜א אֶל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הִנֵּה֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר הַיּ֗וֹם יָשִׁ֤יבוּ לִי֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת מַמְלְכ֥וּת אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: So the king said to Ziba, “All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours!” “I humbly bow before you,” said Ziba. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king!”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Ziba.
King David said, “Everything that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours.”
Ziba replied to King David.
Ziba said, “I bow down before you.”
Ziba said, “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לְצִבָ֔א הִנֵּ֣ה לְךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִמְפִי־ בֹ֑שֶׁת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ הִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֵ֔יתִי אֶמְצָא־ חֵ֥ן בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the family of the house of Saul was just coming out. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and as he approached, he kept yelling out curses.
passages.sermon:
King David came near Bahurim.
A man came out from that place.
This man belonged to the family of Saul.
His name was Shimei.
Shimei was the son of Gera.
Shimei came out as David approached.
Shimei shouted curses as he came.
passages.original: וּבָ֛א הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִ֖ד עַד־ בַּֽחוּרִ֑ים וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשָּׁם֩ אִ֨ישׁ יוֹצֵ֜א מִמִּשְׁפַּ֣חַת בֵּית־ שָׁא֗וּל וּשְׁמוֹ֙ שִׁמְעִ֣י בֶן־ גֵּרָ֔א יֹצֵ֥א יָצ֖וֹא וּמְקַלֵּֽל׃

passages.text: He threw stones at David and at all the servants of the king, though the troops and all the mighty men were on David’s right and left.
passages.sermon:
Shimei was a man from the family of Saul.
He came out as King David approached Bahurim.
Shimei threw stones at David.
He also threw stones at all the king’s servants.
David’s troops stood on his right and left.
All the mighty men were with David.
Shimei threw stones even though the people and the warriors surrounded David.
passages.original: וַיְסַקֵּ֤ל בָּֽאֲבָנִים֙ אֶת־ דָּוִ֔ד וְאֶת־ כָּל־ עַבְדֵ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ וְכָל־ הַגִּבֹּרִ֔ים מִימִינ֖וֹ וּמִשְּׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And as he yelled curses, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you worthless man of bloodshed!
passages.sermon:
Shimei was a man from the family of Saul.
Shimei came out as King David approached Bahurim.
Shimei yelled curses at David.
Shimei said, “Get out! Get out!”
Shimei called David a man of bloodshed.
Shimei called David a worthless man.
passages.original: וְכֹֽה־ אָמַ֥ר שִׁמְעִ֖י בְּקַֽלְל֑וֹ צֵ֥א צֵ֛א אִ֥ישׁ הַדָּמִ֖ים וְאִ֥ישׁ הַבְּלִיָּֽעַל׃

passages.text: The LORD has paid you back for all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, you have come to ruin because you are a man of bloodshed!”
passages.sermon:
Shimei spoke to David.
Shimei said that the LORD has paid David back.
The LORD has paid David for all the blood of Saul’s house.
David ruled in Saul’s place.
The LORD has given the kingdom to Absalom, David’s son.
David is now in trouble.
Shimei said David is a man of bloodshed.
passages.original: הֵשִׁיב֩ עָלֶ֨יךָ יְהוָ֜ה כֹּ֣ל׀ דְּמֵ֣י בֵית־ שָׁא֗וּל אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָלַ֙כְתָּ֙ תַּחְתּוֹ וַיִּתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בְּנֶ֑ךָ וְהִנְּךָ֙ בְּרָ֣עָתֶ֔ךָ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ דָּמִ֖ים אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head!”
passages.sermon:
Abishai was the son of Zeruiah.
Abishai spoke to King David.
Abishai said, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king?”
Abishai said, “Let me go over and cut off his head.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן־ צְרוּיָה֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֣מָּה יְקַלֵּ֞ל הַכֶּ֤לֶב הַמֵּת֙ הַזֶּ֔ה אֶת־ אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ אֶעְבְּרָה־ נָּ֖א וְאָסִ֥ירָה אֶת־ רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃ס

passages.text: But the king replied, “What have I to do with you, O sons of Zeruiah? If he curses me because the LORD told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’ ”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to the sons of Zeruiah.
He said, “What do I have to do with you?”
He said, “Let him curse.”
He said, “The LORD told him to curse David.”
He said, “No one can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מַה־ לִּ֥י וְלָכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י צְרֻיָ֑ה כִּי יְקַלֵּ֗ל וְכִי יְהוָה֙ אָ֤מַר לוֹ֙ קַלֵּ֣ל אֶת־ דָּוִ֔ד וּמִ֣י יֹאמַ֔ר מַדּ֖וּעַ עָשִׂ֥יתָה כֵּֽן׃ס

passages.text: Then David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Behold, my own son, my own flesh and blood, seeks my life. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone and let him curse me, for the LORD has told him so.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to Abishai.
David spoke to all his servants.
David said, “My own son wants to kill me.
My son came from my own body.
He seeks my life.
Now a man from the tribe of Benjamin curses me.
This man is a Benjamite.
Let him alone.
Let him curse me.
The LORD told him to do this.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤ד אֶל־ אֲבִישַׁי֙ וְאֶל־ כָּל־ עֲבָדָ֔יו הִנֵּ֥ה בְנִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־ יָצָ֥א מִמֵּעַ֖י מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֶת־ נַפְשִׁ֑י וְאַ֨ף כִּֽי־ עַתָּ֜ה בֶּן־ הַיְמִינִ֗י הַנִּ֤חוּ לוֹ֙ וִֽיקַלֵּ֔ל כִּ֥י אָֽמַר־ ל֖וֹ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Perhaps the LORD will see my affliction and repay me with good for the cursing I receive today.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David was suffering.
David was being cursed that day.
David said, "Perhaps the LORD will see my trouble."
David said, "Perhaps the LORD will notice my pain."
David said, "Perhaps the LORD will give me good."
David said, "Perhaps the LORD will repay me with blessing."
David said, "Perhaps the LORD will do this because of the curses I receive today."
passages.original: אוּלַ֛י יִרְאֶ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה בְּעֲוֹנִי וְהֵשִׁ֨יב יְהוָ֥ה לִי֙ טוֹבָ֔ה תַּ֥חַת קִלְלָת֖וֹ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: So David and his men proceeded along the road as Shimei went along the ridge of the hill opposite him. As Shimei went, he yelled curses, threw stones, and flung dust at David.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David had loyal men with him.
David and his men walked along the road.
Shimei was a man from the tribe of Benjamin.
Shimei walked on the hillside across from David.
Shimei walked along the ridge, opposite David.
Shimei shouted curses at David.
Shimei threw stones at David.
Shimei flung dust at David.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ דָּוִ֛ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֖יו בַּדָּ֑רֶךְס וְשִׁמְעִ֡י הֹלֵךְ֩ בְּצֵ֨לַע הָהָ֜ר לְעֻמָּת֗וֹ הָלוֹךְ֙ וַיְקַלֵּ֔ל וַיְסַקֵּ֤ל בָּֽאֲבָנִים֙ לְעֻמָּת֔וֹ וְעִפַּ֖ר בֶּעָפָֽר׃פ

passages.text: Finally, the king and all the people with him arrived, exhausted. And there he refreshed himself.
passages.sermon:
David was the king.
David traveled with all the people who were with him.
They arrived at their destination.
They were exhausted.
David rested there.
The people rested there.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָל־ הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֖וֹ עֲיֵפִ֑ים וַיִּנָּפֵ֖שׁ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom led a group of people from Israel.
All the men of Israel came with Absalom.
They entered Jerusalem.
Ahithophel was with Absalom.
Ahithophel was a counselor.
passages.original: וְאַבְשָׁל֗וֹם וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֖אוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַאֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And David’s friend Hushai the Archite went to Absalom and said to him, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
passages.sermon:
Hushai was a friend of David.
Hushai was an Archite.
Hushai went to Absalom.
Hushai spoke to Absalom.
Hushai said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֞א חוּשַׁ֧י הָאַרְכִּ֛י רֵעֶ֥ה דָוִ֖ד אֶל־ אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר חוּשַׁי֙ אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם יְחִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: “Is this the loyalty you show your friend?” Absalom replied. “Why did you not go with your friend?”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of David.
Absalom spoke to Hushai.
Absalom said, “Is this how you show kindness to your friend?”
Absalom asked, “Why did you not go with your friend?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־ חוּשַׁ֔י זֶ֥ה חַסְדְּךָ֖ אֶת־ רֵעֶ֑ךָ לָ֥מָּה לֹֽא־ הָלַ֖כְתָּ אֶת־ רֵעֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: “Not at all,” Hushai answered. “For the one chosen by the LORD, by the people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and with him I will remain.
passages.sermon:
Hushai was a friend of David.
Absalom was David’s son.
Hushai spoke to Absalom.
Hushai answered Absalom.
Hushai said, “No, that is not true.”
The LORD chose someone to be king.
The people chose him also.
All the men of Israel chose him.
I will serve the one whom the LORD, the people, and all Israel have chosen.
I will stay with him.
I will remain with him.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁי֮ אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלֹם֒ לֹ֕א כִּי֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּחַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה וְהָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה וְכָל־ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹא אֶהְיֶ֖ה וְאִתּ֥וֹ אֵשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: Furthermore, whom should I serve if not the son? As I served in your father’s presence, so also I will serve in yours.”
passages.sermon:
Hushai spoke to Absalom.
Hushai said, “Who should I serve?”
Hushai said, “I will serve the son.”
Hushai had served Absalom’s father, King David, before.
Hushai said, “As I served your father, I will serve you.”
passages.original: וְהַשֵּׁנִ֗ית לְמִי֙ אֲנִ֣י אֶֽעֱבֹ֔ד הֲל֖וֹא לִפְנֵ֣י בְנ֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָבַ֙דְתִּי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ כֵּ֖ן אֶהְיֶ֥ה לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃פ

passages.text: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give me counsel. What should we do?”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Ahithophel was a trusted advisor.
Absalom spoke to Ahithophel.
Absalom said, “Give us advice.”
Absalom asked, “What should we do?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל־ אֲחִיתֹ֑פֶל הָב֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם עֵצָ֖ה מַֽה־ נַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: Ahithophel replied, “Sleep with your father’s concubines, whom he has left to keep the palace. When all Israel hears that you have become a stench to your father, then the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.”
passages.sermon:
Ahithophel was a trusted advisor.
Ahithophel spoke to Absalom.
Ahithophel said, “Go to your father’s concubines.
Your father left these women to keep the palace.
All Israel will hear what you have done.
They will know you have made yourself hateful to your father.
Then everyone with you will become stronger.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲחִיתֹ֙פֶל֙ אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם בּ֚וֹא אֶל־ פִּלַגְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִנִּ֖יחַ לִשְׁמ֣וֹר הַבָּ֑יִת וְשָׁמַ֤ע כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּֽי־ נִבְאַ֣שְׁתָּ אֶת־ אָבִ֔יךָ וְחָ֣זְק֔וּ יְדֵ֖י כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom rebelled against his father David.
Absalom’s followers set up a tent for him on the roof of the palace.
Absalom went into his father’s concubines.
All Israel saw what Absalom did.
passages.original: וַיַּטּ֧וּ לְאַבְשָׁל֛וֹם הָאֹ֖הֶל עַל־ הַגָּ֑ג וַיָּבֹ֤א אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־ פִּֽלַגְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֔יו לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Now in those days the advice of Ahithophel was like the consultation of the word of God. Such was the regard that both David and Absalom had for Ahithophel’s advice.
passages.sermon:
Ahithophel was a counselor in Israel.
He gave advice to others.
In those days, people respected his advice very much.
They thought his advice was like asking for the word of God.
David trusted Ahithophel’s advice.
Absalom also trusted Ahithophel’s advice.
Both David and Absalom valued what Ahithophel said.
passages.original: וַעֲצַ֣ת אֲחִיתֹ֗פֶל אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָעַץ֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשְׁאַלִ֖־ בִּדְבַ֣ר הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כֵּ֚ן כָּל־ עֲצַ֣ת אֲחִיתֹ֔פֶל גַּם־ לְדָוִ֖ד גַּ֥ם לְאַבְשָׁלֹֽם׃ס
